name: Next Up Cleanup
description: Clears the first episodes of never-started series out of Next Up and collapses duplicate episodes of one series in Continue Watching, so both rows only hold shows you are actually watching. Filtering changes no watch data; an opt-in scheduled task can also clear the play state of barely-started episodes.
overview: Next Up without the first episode of every show you never started, and Continue Watching without the same show four times.

versions.changelog: Adds the toggle script the way Jellyfin Enhanced does - its own middleware, registered as a singleton start-up filter - and drops the File Transformation route 1.3.0.1 tried. Both earlier attempts took index.html down with an ObjectDisposedException raised inside File Transformation 2.5.11.0, which resolves services lazily from a provider that is disposed after start-up; registering a transformation hits that directly, and adding a transient start-up filter disturbed start-up enough to hit it indirectly. Jellyfin Enhanced has used a singleton start-up filter alongside the same File Transformation build for a long time without trouble, so this follows it exactly.

DO NOT INSTALL - this build takes the web client down with an HTTP 500 on servers running File Transformation 2.5.11.0. Use 1.3.0.2 or later. Fixes 1.3.0.0 returning HTTP 500 for the web client. That release added its toggle script by registering ASP.NET middleware through an IStartupFilter; on Jellyfin 10.11.11 a plugin doing that breaks the static-file pipeline, and every request for index.html failed with an ObjectDisposedException whether or not the toggle was switched on. The script is now added through the File Transformation plugin instead - the same mechanism Home Screen Sections and Plugin Pages use - and no middleware is registered at all. If File Transformation is not installed the toggle simply does not appear and everything else is unaffected. Anyone on 1.3.0.0 should update or roll back.

DO NOT INSTALL - this build returns HTTP 500 for the web client on Jellyfin 10.11.11 and cannot be disabled from its settings. Use 1.3.0.1 or later. Adds a per-series toggle to series pages in the web client, next to Play. Switching a series off removes every one of its episodes from Next Up and Continue Watching outright - episode number, play state, resume position and the started-watching mark all stop applying to it. Each user has their own list and the server reads the user from the request's own token, so switching a series off never changes what anybody else sees, and because the filtering is server-side the series is gone from those rows on every client, not just the browser it was switched off in. The button is added by a script injected into index.html at request time, so nothing is written into the web folder for a jellyfin-web update to wipe.

Corrects the plugin's own description and the top of the configuration page, which both still promised that no watch data is ever touched. That stopped being true when the opt-in Reset abandoned episodes task landed in 1.2.0.0, since deleting play state is what that task is for. Filtering still changes nothing, so that is what they now say, naming the task as the one exception. No behaviour changes.

Fixes the Reset abandoned episodes task failing immediately on Jellyfin 10.11.11 with a MissingMethodException. IUserManager.Users was a property up to 10.11.3 and is a GetUsers() method from 10.11.11, so one plugin binary cannot bind to either at compile time and still run on both halves of the 10.11 series. The user list is now asked for in whichever way the running server offers it. Filtering was never affected.

Adds a threshold under which an episode counts as never started. Jellyfin writes a resume position, a play count and a play date on the very first frame, so a mis-tap or a stopped auto-play was enough to pin an episode to a row for good. An episode now counts as watched only if it is marked played or its resume position is past the mark - five minutes by default, configurable. A bare play count or play date no longer counts for anything. Also new: an opt-in Reset abandoned episodes scheduled task that clears the play state of episodes stopped before a second, lower mark (two minutes by default), for tidying the database behind the rows. It skips anything marked played, deletes watch data, cannot be undone, and never runs unless you start it by hand.

Two fixes for a first episode surviving in a merged Continue Watching / Next Up row. Such a row is protected from losing an episode you are part-way through, but that protection was reading any play state at all as "part-way through" - so an S01E01 with a play count and a play date but no resume position stayed put, which is precisely the entry the row should not have. Only a resume position counts now: an episode you actually paused is still never removed, while one that was finished, or started and abandoned, is. Separately, the What to hide setting rendered blank after saving and silently reset itself on the next save, because the page offered the mode as a number while the server returns its name.

Rows are now filtered as the controller's own result, before anything is serialised, instead of by rewriting the response body. That is what makes it work everywhere: it no longer depends on the client's JSON casing profile or on response compression, and it reaches rows built by plugin controllers such as the Home Screen Sections plugin, which the 1.0 middleware could miss entirely. New: Continue Watching is deduplicated, so a series you skipped around in collapses to the episode you played most recently. An unrecognised row endpoint now names itself in the debug log.

Filters the combined Continue Watching / Next Up home row, which 1.0.0.0 missed: the Continue Watching endpoints and any Home Screen Sections section are now covered, not just /Shows/NextUp. On a combined row only untouched first episodes are hidden, so an episode you are part-way through never disappears. Routes behind a reverse proxy base path are matched too, and every filtered row is logged at debug level.

Initial release: filters the first episodes of never-started series out of Next Up, on every client, without touching any watch data. Two modes - hide every S01E01, or keep the ones that already have a resume position or a play date. Requests are over-fetched and trimmed so the row stays as long as the client asked for.
